questions.question: How does CSS specificity work? Explain the rules with examples.
questions.title: CSS Specificity Explained — Rules, Calculation & !important
questions.direct_answer:
How does CSS specificity work? Explain the rules with examples.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Specificity tuple (inline, IDs, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, elements/pseudo-elements); !important and cascade layers; source order tiebreaker.

**Classic weak answer:** Relying on !important to win — makes future overrides harder; better to adjust selectors or use cascade layers (@layer).

**Senior finish:** Introduce @layer (CSS cascade layers) as the modern way to manage specificity across design systems.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **CSS Specificity Explained — Rules, Calculation & !important** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** How does CSS specificity work? Explain the rules with examples.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Specificity tuple (inline, IDs, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, elements/pseudo-elements); !important and cascade layers; source order tiebreaker**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Relying on !important to win — makes future overrides harder; better to adjust selectors or use cascade layers (@layer)**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Introduce @layer (CSS cascade layers) as the modern way to manage specificity across design systems**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Specificity tuple (inline, IDs, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, elements/pseudo-elements); !important and cascade layers; source order tiebreaker
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **relying on !important to win — makes future overrides harder; better to adjust selectors or use cascade layers (@layer)** and what you do instead.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **Specificity tuple (inline, IDs, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, elements/pseudo-elements); !important and cascade layers; source order tiebreaker** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

questions.question: What is the CSS box model? Explain content-box vs border-box.
questions.title: CSS Box Model Explained — content-box vs border-box
questions.direct_answer:
What is the CSS box model? Explain content-box vs border-box.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Content/padding/border/margin layers; box-sizing controls whether padding/border are included in width/height; * { box-sizing: border-box } is standard.

**Classic weak answer:** Forgetting box-sizing: border-box is not the default — width in content-box excludes padding and border, causing layout surprises.

**Senior finish:** Show the universal reset (* { box-sizing: border-box }), mention margin collapsing quirks, and note border-box is essential for predictable layout.
